questions.qtext:
Consider a $256$ KB $4$-way set associative cache with $256$ byte cache lines for a processor that uses $64$-bit data words and $48$-bit byte addresses. Assume the variable x, of type uint64_t, is stored in memory at location 0x4A85 B413 A518. (uint64_t means an unsigned $64$-bit integer)
Assume that x is present in the cache, and char* ptr $=0 \times 4 \mathrm{~A} 85$ B400 0000. (Note: sizeof(char) = 1)

Consider the accesses in the following options. For each access, it can be a MISS or HIT or NOT ENOUGH INFO. For each access, it is a MISS if it "must" cause a miss, HIT if it will "never" cause a miss, or NOT ENOUGH INFO.
Determine which of the following accesses will cause a cache HIT.
questions.solution:
Answer: B

Source solution 1 (score: 4)
$$
\begin{array}{llll}
*\left(\mathrm{ptr}+0 \times 11_A538\right) & \text{MISS} & \text{HIT} & \text{(NOT ENOUGH INFO)} \\
*\left(\mathrm{ptr}+0 \times 13_A588\right) & \text{MISS} & \text{(HIT)} & \text{NOT ENOUGH INFO} \\
*\left(\mathrm{ptr}+0 \times 13_0218\right) & \text{MISS} & \text{HIT} & \text{(NOT ENOUGH INFO)} \\
\end{array}
$$

* (ptr + 0x11_A538) is in the same set but has a different tag, it may or may not be in another way in that set. *(ptr + 0x13_A588) is in same the line as $x$ (it is in the same set and has the same tag), and since $x$ in present in the cache, it must be also. *(ptr + 0x13_0218) has the same tag, but is in a different set, so it may or may not be in the cache.
Source solution 2 (score: 0)

Based on the problem statement and the cache configuration provided in the image, here is the step-by-step solution to determine which access will result in a guaranteed cache HIT.

1. Analyze the Cache Configuration

First, we need to break down how the 48-bit physical address is interpreted by the cache.

  • Block Offset:

    • Block Size = $256$ bytes = $2^8$ bytes.

    • Offset Bits = 8 bits (Corresponds to the last 2 Hex digits).

  • Set Index:

    • Number of Sets = $\frac{\text{Cache Size}}{\text{Associativity} \times \text{Block Size}}$

    • Number of Sets = $\frac{256 \text{ KB}}{4 \times 256 \text{ Bytes}} = \frac{256 \times 1024}{1024} = 256 \text{ Sets}$.

    • Index Bits = $\log_2(256) = \mathbf{8 \text{ bits}}$ (Corresponds to the 2 Hex digits preceding the offset).

  • Tag:

    • Remaining bits = $48 - (8 \text{ Index} + 8 \text{ Offset}) = 32$ bits.

    • Tag Bits = 32 bits (Corresponds to the first 8 Hex digits).

Address Structure (Hexadecimal):

[ Tag (8 digits) ] [ Index (2 digits) ] [ Offset (2 digits) ]

2. Analyze the Address of Variable x

We are told that variable x is present in the cache. This means the specific cache block containing x is loaded. For another access to be a guaranteed HIT, it must target the exact same block (i.e., it must have the exact same Tag and Index).

  • Address of x: 0x4A85 B413 A518

  • Breakdown:

    • Offset: 18 (Last 2 digits)

    • Index: A5 (Next 2 digits)

    • Tag: 4A85 B413 (First 8 digits)

Condition for HIT: The target address must have Tag = 4A85 B413 and Index = A5.

3. Evaluate the Options

We need to calculate the address for each option by adding the offset to the base pointer ptr.

Base ptr address: 0x4A85 B400 0000

Option A: *(ptr + 0x11A538)

  • Calculation: 0x4A85 B400 0000 + 0x11A538 = 0x4A85 B411 A538

  • Breakdown:

    • Offset: 38

    • Index: A5 (Matches x)

    • Tag: 4A85 B411 (Mismatch with x's tag 4A85 B413)

  • Result: Different block. No guaranteed HIT.

Option B: *(ptr + 0x13A588)

  • Calculation: 0x4A85 B400 0000 + 0x13A588 = 0x4A85 B413 A588

  • Breakdown:

    • Offset: 88

    • Index: A5 (Matches x)

    • Tag: 4A85 B413 (Matches x)

  • Result: This address maps to the exact same cache block as x. Since x is present, this block is present. Guaranteed HIT.

Option C: *(ptr + 0x130218)

  • Calculation: 0x4A85 B400 0000 + 0x130218 = 0x4A85 B413 0218

  • Breakdown:

    • Offset: 18

    • Index: 02 (Mismatch with x's index A5)

    • Tag: 4A85 B413

  • Result: Different set. No guaranteed HIT.

Conclusion

Only the address in Option B has the same Tag and Set Index as variable x. Therefore, it accesses the same cache block that is already known to be in the cache.

Correct Answer: B

Source solution 3 (score: 0)

Address Space: 48 bits

Block Size (Line Size): 256 bytes = $2^8$ bytes $\implies$ 8 bits for Block Offset

Cache Size: 256 KB = $2^{18}$ bytes

Total Blocks in Cache: $\frac{256\text{ KB}}{256\text{ B}} = 1024$ blocks

Associativity: 4-way set associative $\implies$ Each set contains 4 blocks.

Total Sets in Cache: $\frac{1024\text{ blocks}}{4} = 256 = 2^8$ sets $\implies$ 8 bits for Set Index

Now we find the Tag bits:

$$\text{Tag bits} = 48 - (\text{Set Index bits} + \text{Block Offset bits}) = 48 - (8 + 8) = 32\text{ bits}$$

$$\text{Address Format: } \underbrace{\texttt{T T T T T T T T}}_{32\text{ bits (Tag)}} \ \underbrace{\texttt{S S}}_{8\text{ bits (Set)}} \ \underbrace{\texttt{O O}}_{8\text{ bits (Offset)}}$$

in hexadecimal format

We know the variable x is currently present in the cache at address 0x4A85 B413 A518. Let's parse it:

  • Tag: 4A85B413

  • Set Index: A5

  • Block Offset: 18

Because x is guaranteed to be in the cache, anyy future access that maps to this exact same Tag and Set Index will cause a Cache HIT.

Given the base pointer: ptr = 0x4A85 B400 0000

Option A

$$\text{Address} = \texttt{0x4A85 B400 0000} + \texttt{0x11 A538} = \texttt{0x4A85 B411 A538}$$

  • Tag: 4A85B411 (Mismatch)

  • Set Index: A5

  • Result: MISS

Option B

$$\text{Address} = \texttt{0x4A85 B400 0000} + \texttt{0x13 A588} = \texttt{0x4A85 B413 A588}$$

  • Tag: 4A85B413 ($\color{green}{\text{Matches!}}$)

  • Set Index: A5 ($\color{green}{\text{Matches!}}$)

  • Result: HIT (Since it targets the exact same memory block currently holding x).

Option C

$$\text{Address} = \texttt{0x4A85 B400 0000} + \texttt{0x13 0218} = \texttt{0x4A85 B413 0218}$$

  • Tag: 4A85B413

  • Set Index: 02 (Mismatch)

  • Result: MISS

questions.qtext: A direct-mapped cache has $64$ blocks and a block size of $16$ bytes. To what block number in the cache does byte address $1220_{10}$ map?
questions.solution:
Answer: C

Source solution 1 (score: 7)
First find the main memory block number to which the byte address 1220 belongs to, which can be found by $1220 / 16$, so, block number 76 (NOTE that block numbers start with 0 ).

Now, block number 76 maps to line number $76 \% 64=12$.
Source solution 2 (score: 4)

Answer: 12

Easiest Explaination:

\[
\text{Number of bits for block offset} = \log_2(16) = 4 \text{ bits}
\]

\[
\text{Number of bits for line number} = \log_2(64) = 6 \text{ bits}
\]

\[
(1220)_{10} = (10011000100)_2
\]

\[
\text{Address format: } \quad 1 \;|\; 001100 \;|\; 0100
\]

\[
\text{Line number} = (001100)_2 = (12)_{10}
\]

Source solution 3 (score: 1)

  • Question: Block number for address 1220 (64 blocks, 16B block size).

  • Calc:

    1. Block Address = $1220 / 16 = 76$ (integer division).

    2. Cache Block Number = $76 \pmod{64} = 12$.

  • Answer: C. 12

questions.qtext: The size of the physical address space of a processor is $2^P$ bytes. The word length is $2^W$ bytes. The capacity of cache memory is $2^N$ bytes. The size of each cache block is $2^M$ words. For a $K$-way set-associative cache memory, the length (in number of bits) of the tag field is
questions.solution:
Answer: B

Source solution 1 (score: 4)
$\text{Physical Address Space} =2^P$ Bytes, i.e., $P$ bits to represent the size of total memory.

$\text{Cache Size} = 2^N$ Bytes, i.e., $N$ bits to represent Cache memory.

$\text{Tag size} = 2^X$ Bytes, i.e., $X$ bits to represent Tag.

Cache is $K-$way associative.

$\text{(Size of Tag)} \times \frac{\text{Cache Size}}{K} = \text{Total Memory Size}$

$\implies 2^X \times \frac{2^N}{K} = 2^P $

$\implies 2^{X+N-\log(K)} = 2^P $

$\implies 2^{X} = 2^{P-N+\log(K)} $

$\implies X (\text{Size of Tag in bits}) = P - N + \log(K)$

Correct Answer: $B$
Source solution 2 (score: 0)

Answer: (B)

\[
\begin{aligned}
\textbf{Physical Address Bits:} \quad
& \log_2(2^P) = P \\[6pt]

\textbf{Block Size:} \quad
& 2^M \text{ words} = 2^M \cdot 2^W = 2^{M+W} \\
& \Rightarrow \text{Block offset bits} = M + W \\[6pt]

\textbf{Number of Lines:} \quad
& \frac{2^N}{2^{M+W}} = 2^{N - M - W} \\[6pt]

\textbf{K-way Set Associative Cache:} \quad
& \text{Number of sets} = \frac{2^{N - M - W}}{K} \\
& \Rightarrow \text{Set index bits} = \log_2\left(\frac{2^{N - M - W}}{K}\right) \\
& = N - M - W - \log_2 K \\[6pt]

\textbf{Let Tag Bits} = x \\[6pt]

\textbf{Address Breakdown:} \quad
& x + \text{Set bits} + \text{Offset bits} = P \\
& x + (N - M - W - \log_2 K) + (M + W) = P \\[6pt]

\textbf{Final Result:} \quad
& x = P - N + \log_2 K
\end{aligned}
\]

Source solution 3 (score: 0)
